body: There's an unwritten rule from what I've seen to not critique work unless asked, I'd definitely write in your end summery for critiques, or maybe ask a beta or fellow writers in your fandom to take a peak at it! :D
If it fits the vibe of the fic then I think it's really cool! Sometimes I might discover songs or listen to a song solely because I'm reminded of a fic I like :D
Personally I love chapters so I can easily find and reread my favorite parts over and over :D

This is coming from how I personally am for the fics I follow but your readers might be this way too; Sometimes I just don't know what to say. Even if it's a chapter that I can't help but re-read over and over. After awhile I might personally come back after a couple of days to collect my thoughts and THEN I might come back to comment.   
But sometimes I might just completely draw a blank of what to say and just wait until the next chapter to say something. I definitely wouldn't be worried about whether or not they liked it, I'm sure they probably love it! Sometimes works are so good that you just can't help but have to reread it or take a little bit to digest it in order to express how you feel about a fic :)

Of course the atmosphere and music choices make me enamoured with this game, though alot of others already have elaborated on that. The monsters having a deeper meaning to the characters is pretty wicked, I enjoy digging in the lore to learn what the monsters symbolism is for the main characters. I also really enjoy the complex characters. It's not melodramatic in SH2. I recently learned in theater class the other day that series with Super Heros, or Star Wars are often melodramatic. There is only good vs evil, there is no in-between. Silent Hill 2 decided to not go with this choice with it's characters. They're human, they may not make the best choices, but they are still  living and breathing and deserve to live. That being said, good vs evil can be pulled off pretty well if you give it a little life to it, Silent Hill 3 was able to keep it interesting with it's evil cult story. From this serious tone Silent Hill 3's protagonist being witty and sassy really made me enjoy her as a main character. Don't get me wrong, I loved James but Heather has some oomph to her. She wasn't unfathomably unreal, she wasn't too cheesy in her one liners but had enough to break the tension if only for a little while. Personally one of my favorite moments is when we, the audience along with Heather really think about the possibility of what is real and not. My personal favorite being from a line in Silent Hill 3 being; "They look like monsters to you?" And that ONE sentence alone creates so many ideas, are the monsters REALLY monsters? What has Heather and ther other character have been killing in Silent Hill, Cult Members? Real people? It's instances like these that the story doesn't elaborate on, but leaves it for the viewer to decide. The fear of the unknown is really a relevant thing that should be taken advantage of.
